title: Quantum channels on duals of von Neumann algebras in the Schrödinger picture
abstract: The theory of quantum channels is traditionally studied either on finite-dimensional state spaces or within the Heisenberg picture as completely positive maps on C^*-algebras. In this paper, we consider quantum channels as completely positive maps on the duals of general von Neumann algebras in the Schrodinger picture. We investigate the construction of such channels through Pettis integrals using representations of topological groups.
summary: This paper develops a general theory for quantum channels acting on the state spaces associated with von Neumann algebras in the Schrödinger picture. It achieves this by constructing these channels as Pettis integrals involving unitary representations over topological groups. This mathematical generalization allows the framework to handle complex, infinite-dimensional open quantum systems beyond traditional finite-dimensional models.
main_problem: The paper extends the study of quantum channels from finite-dimensional state spaces or the Heisenberg picture to the duals of general von Neumann algebras in the Schrödinger picture.
main_result: Quantum channels can be systematically constructed as completely positive maps on $M^*$ via Pettis integrals involving representations of topological groups, and these constructions preserve semigroup properties under convolution semigroups of measures.
method: The core method involves defining quantum channels $\Phi: M^* 	o M^*$ using the integral form $\int_G \pi(g)ho\pi(g)^* d\mu(g)$, which generalizes unitary averaging techniques to infinite dimensions.
model_or_system: The model concerns open quantum systems whose dynamics are described by completely positive maps (quantum channels) acting on the state space $\Sigma(M)$ associated with an infinite-dimensional von Neumann algebra $M \subset B(H)$.
key_observables: Quantum states $ho \in \Sigma(M)$, observables $A \in M$, and the action of the channel $\Phi$ on these elements.
important_parameters: The structure of the underlying topological group $G$ and the measure $\mu$ used in the Pettis integral construction are critical parameters.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the dynamics can be modeled by averaging unitaries derived from representations $\pi: G 	o U(H)$; a key limitation noted is the potential failure of SOT-continuity for such representations.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon known results for finite systems, introduces the general framework on $M^*$, proves that unitary evolution and Pettis integral constructions yield valid channels (Theorems 3.1 & 3.2), and then explores semigroup properties using convolution semigroups of measures.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical framework for describing open quantum system dynamics in infinite dimensions by generalizing standard channel definitions to the dual space, which is crucial for modern theoretical treatments of continuous systems.
